text:
Launchstack

 A TypeScript engine for AI-native applications. Ingestion, OCR, RAG, knowledge graph, LLM abstractions, and background jobs — ports-based, and wired into a Next.js reference app that shows how the pieces fit together.

 
 
 

Self-host · Develop · Repository layout · Packages · Architecture · Chat models · Contributing

---

 Status

The publishable bricks in packages/ and the compositions package @launchstack/pipelines are not yet on npm . The engine aggregate is @launchstack/engine ; @launchstack/design-tokens is private. The first release will publish the public packages together through the Changesets flow in release.yml , which builds the bricks and pipelines, validates the packed engine tarball with publint , and checks every declared publishable subpath for Node-ESM loadability. Until that first release lands, consume the engine by running this repository.

To try Launchstack today, run the app below.

---

 Self-host in two commands

All the machine needs is Docker. No clone, no Node, no hand-edited .env .

 

 

 setup asks where people will reach the instance (this machine, your domain, or a bare public IP), for a chat model key and an embeddings key, generates every secret, checks the configuration, pulls the published images and starts the stack, with automatic HTTPS when you gave it a domain. Open the address it prints and create your account.

Afterwards: launchstack status , logs , doctor , update , backup and restore . The full guide is docs/self-hosting.md.

---

 Run it locally

This is the path for working on Launchstack itself or running unreleased code. To just run an instance, use the two commands above.

 Requirements: Node ≥ 20 and pnpm 10.15.1 ( corepack enable picks up the pinned version).

 

 apps/web/src/env.ts refuses to boot without DATABASE URL and BETTER AUTH SECRET . Compose supplies the database, file storage, and every local service; .env.example already points DATABASE URL at it. A usable instance — sign-up, searchable uploads, chat — needs these in .env :

 Variable Value 
 --- --- 
 BETTER AUTH SECRET openssl rand -base64 32 
 BETTER AUTH URL (the .env.example default). Without it, browser sign-up is refused with "Invalid origin". 
 Chat Gemini: GOOGLE AI API KEY , with CHAT BASE URL unset. Azure OpenAI: CHAT BASE URL=https:// .openai.azure.com/openai/v1 , CHAT API KEY , and CHAT MODELS CONFIG=config/chat-models.azure.yaml . See Chat models. 
 Embeddings EMBEDDING API BASE URL + EMBEDDING API KEY . There is no default : without them, uploads are read and chunked but never become searchable. Azure OpenAI fits the default EMBEDDING INDEX ( legacy-openai-1536 ) as-is, with text-embedding-3-large deployed under that name. Gemini needs EMBEDDING INDEX=gemini-embedding-768 on a fresh database. 

There is no per-vendor variable: a bare OPENAI API KEY , OPENROUTER API KEY or OLLAMA BASE URL will not configure chat, and none of them is forwarded to the Gemini default — every one of those providers speaks the OpenAI chat-completions protocol, so each is reached through CHAT BASE URL . Only AI BASE URL / AI API KEY , a straight rename of the canonical pair, is still translated for a release with a deprecation warning.

 With Docker (recommended)

 

 make up also exists but runs in the foreground — you will need a second shell to run make down . Use make up-prod unless you want to watch the build. make up-fast builds Next.js on the host first and is the quickest iteration loop.

 Without Docker

You need a Postgres with the pgvector extension available — the migration
runner enables it and exits non-zero on stock Postgres.

 

 web dev is plain next dev — it accepts uploads but processes nothing.
Run the worker alongside it or documents will sit queued forever; the
Inngest dev server is only needed for the Inngest-hosted background
verticals (trend search, prospector, …), not for ingestion.

 db:migrate is the same command CI, Docker and the production image build run.
Running it from @launchstack/store applies only the engine set — that is what a
consumer embedding the engine uses, not what a full app needs.
Nothing else creates schema — see Changing the database.

 db:seed also works against the Compose database. Its accounts sign in at
 /signin with the DEV SEED PASSWORD you passed.

 .env.example points DATABASE URL at localhost:5433/pdr ai v2 , which is what Compose publishes — so the Docker and non-Docker paths share one database by default. Running your own Postgres instead? Use the commented localhost:5432/pdr ai line in its place.

 
 Windows (no make ) 

 

Or install make via Chocolatey ( choco install make ) or Scoop ( scoop install make ).

 

 The repository root is not an application. It is a pnpm workspace: no runtime dependencies, no server, no app code. pnpm dev at the root fails with ERR PNPM NO SCRIPT — always target a package with --filter . Only repo-wide commands live at the root: lint , lint:fix , typecheck , check , format:write , format:check , and the Changesets scripts.

See CONTRIBUTING.md for the full dev guide.

 Self-hosting

A deployment is self-hosted unless you set DEPLOYMENT MODE=cloud , and the
defaults are chosen for that case: usage is recorded but never gated, no
telemetry is loaded, no assets are fetched from a CDN, and the instance
identifies itself by the host you serve it from. Whoever signs up owns the
workspace they create, already verified — there is no separate admin bootstrap.
Sign-up is open to anyone who can reach the instance; see the
self-hosting guide before putting one on a public address.

This repository builds the application. The marketing site at launchstack.app is
a separate app ( apps/landing ) that Docker and Compose do not
build — on your own instance, / is the sign-in page, not a pitch.

Install, update, backup and troubleshooting are in the
self-hosting guide. What degrades without which
optional service is in
Self-hosting defaults.

usage.title: Using the engine standalone
usage.html:
@launchstack/engine is the one-install aggregate: createEngine(CoreConfig) assembles the engine spine and re-exports selected runtime, database, conversion, indexing and orchestration APIs. Import model, OCR, embedding and retrieval APIs from their owning bricks' public subpaths; individual bricks can also be consumed separately. CI checks the declared publishable subpaths under plain Node ESM (scripts/ci/check-package-exports.mjs). The engine package reads no process.env (lint-enforced) — configuration arrives through CoreConfig, typed ports and separate configure* hooks; apps/web/src/server/engine.ts is the reference composition root.

One tenancy caveat remains by design: the engine's search contract is keyed on companyId, so a consumer adopts that workspace model (without inheriting auth, billing, or product tables). See REPOSITORY.md.
